facts.text: An open-source simulator is a simulation program whose source code anyone may read, change and use without paying a license fee, under conditions set by its license.
facts.quote: An open-source simulator is a simulation program whose source code anyone may read, change and use without paying a license fee, under conditions set by its license.

facts.text: The named open-source licenses are permissive: MIT for CARLA's code, BSD-3 for Project Chrono, and Apache 2.0 for Isaac Sim and Gazebo.
facts.quote: The licenses the booklet names are all "permissive": MIT (CARLA's code), BSD-3 (Project Chrono) and Apache 2.0 (Isaac Sim, Gazebo).

facts.text: MIT, BSD-3 and Apache 2.0 allow companies to use, modify and redistribute software, including inside commercial products, provided the original copyright notice is kept.
facts.quote: all three let a company use, modify and redistribute the software, including inside a commercial product, as long as the original copyright notice is kept

facts.text: Apache 2.0 includes an explicit patent grant.
facts.quote: Apache 2.0 also includes an explicit patent grant.

facts.text: MIT, BSD-3 and Apache 2.0 do not require a company to publish its own changes.
facts.quote: None requires the company to publish its own changes.

facts.text: CARLA is a driving simulator on the Unreal game engine and has included a mining earth-mover asset since December 2024.
facts.quote: CARLA (a driving simulator on the Unreal game engine, with a mining earth-mover asset since December 2024)

facts.text: NVIDIA Isaac Sim provides robotics simulation with ray-traced lidar and radar.
facts.quote: NVIDIA Isaac Sim (robotics simulation with ray-traced lidar and radar)

facts.text: Project Chrono is a physics engine for wheeled, tracked and articulated vehicles on deformable terrain.
facts.quote: Project Chrono (a physics engine for wheeled, tracked and articulated vehicles on deformable terrain)

facts.text: Gazebo is a robotics simulator with a long-term release supported to 2031.
facts.quote: Gazebo (a robotics simulator with a long-term release supported to 2031)

facts.text: Scenic is a scenario language named among the booklet's open-source simulation tools.
MineSim is a test system for autonomous trucks in open-pit mines, built from two real mines.
facts.quote: MineSim (a test system for autonomous trucks in open-pit mines, built from two real mines)

facts.text: AutoDRIVE is a digital-twin framework used in an off-road braking study.
facts.quote: AutoDRIVE (a digital-twin framework used in an off-road braking study)

facts.text: MAVS is a university off-road simulation library.
facts.quote: MAVS, a university off-road simulation library

facts.text: Isaac Sim's core uses Apache 2.0, but some assets carry other terms and redistribution with certain components requires a paid enterprise license.
facts.quote: Isaac Sim's core is Apache 2.0, but some assets carry other terms, redistribution with certain components needs a paid enterprise license

facts.text: Vendor staff described free use of Isaac Sim for teams of up to two people.

facts.text: Open-source projects change fast; CARLA changed game engine between release lines, so a frozen, qualified build is advisable.

facts.text: The research did not examine who funds and maintains the open-source projects or how quickly those projects patch security problems.

facts.text: The booklet concludes that open source is viable for a low-license-cost core but is not the lowest-total-cost option: someone must still build and maintain the coupling, assets, scenario database and validation evidence, with no vendor support.
